papers.title: Pseudocompact MAD families under $\mathfrak b=\mathfrak c$
papers.abstract: We prove that if the bounding number $\mathfrak b$ equals the cardinality of the continuum $\mathfrak c$, then every infinite almost disjoint family of size less than $\mathfrak c$ can be extended to a maximal almost disjoint family whose Isbell--Mr\'owka space has a pseudocompact Vietoris hyperspace.

papers.title: Geometric state space, memory representation and architectures
papers.abstract: We introduce a geometric framework for deriving attention architectures. A sequence forms a memory $m\in M_n$, and an attention pairing $\rho_n\colon M_n\to\operatorname{Hom}(A,A)$ determines how that memory acts on each token state. Different representations of this action recover familiar architectures: softmax attention reads individual key--value pairs, linear attention accumulates their contributions in matrix statistics, and Intention fits a regression map from keys to values. The framework also suggests new architectures by changing the geometry of the query--key pairing, the function carried by each value, or the space representing the memory. ImageNet-1K experiments illustrate these constructions through geometric CAFormer variants, a ViT with query-dependent values, and a linear ViT with a wider memory representation.

papers.title: Euclidean interval objects in categories with finite products
papers.abstract: Based on the intuitive notion of convexity, we formulate a universal property defining interval objects in a category with finite products. Interval objects are structures corresponding to closed intervals of the real line, but their definition does not assume a pre-existing notion of real number. The universal property characterises such structures up to isomorphism, supports the definition of functions between intervals, and provides a means of verifying identities between functions. In the category of sets, the universal property characterises closed intervals of real numbers with nonempty interior. In the category of topological spaces, we obtain intervals with the Euclidean topology. We also prove that every elementary topos with natural numbers object contains an interval object; furthermore, we characterise interval objects as intervals of real numbers in the Cauchy completion of the rational numbers within the Dedekind reals.

papers.title: On rough ideal convergence
papers.abstract: We continue the study of ideal convergence for sequences $(x_n)$ with values in a topological space $X$ with respect to a family $\{F_\eta:\eta\in X\}$ of subsets of $X$ with $\eta\in F_\eta$, where each $F_\eta$ measures the allowed ``roughness'' of convergence toward $\eta$. More precisely, after introducing the corresponding notions of cluster and limit points, we prove several inclusion and invariance properties, discuss their structural properties, and give examples showing that the rough notions are genuinely different from the classical ideal ones.

papers.title: Prime Density, Kolmogorov Quotients and Homeomorphisms between Mac\'ias Spaces of Integral Domains
papers.abstract: For an integral domain $R$ that is not a field, the Mac\'ias space $M(R)$ is the topological space whose underlying set $R^0=R\setminus\{0\}$ is endowed with the topology generated by the basis $\{\sigma_k^0:k\in R^0\}$, where $\sigma_k^0=\{x\in R^0:\langle x\rangle+\langle k\rangle=R\}$. We characterize the openness of the unit group in $M(R)$ via semiprimitivity and, for Dedekind domains and unique factorization domains (UFDs), relate semiprimitivity and the infinitude of prime elements to the density of irreducible and prime elements. We identify the Kolmogorov quotient of $M(R)$ with a space of sets of maximal ideals and reduce the homeomorphism problem to these quotients and the cardinalities of the fibers of the quotient maps; in particular, local domains of equal cardinality have homeomorphic Mac\'ias spaces. For Dedekind domains, we solve this problem in terms of the cardinalities of their unit groups and relations among the ideal classes of their maximal ideals, thereby answering the homeomorphism problem of Mac\'ias (2024) for countable semiprimitive ones. When the class groups are torsion, as they are for principal ideal domains, the cardinalities of the unit groups and of the sets of maximal ideals suffice. For UFDs, we characterize homeomorphic Mac\'ias spaces via comaximality with prime elements and, under an additional hypothesis, obtain a solution analogous to that for Dedekind domains. We solve the problem for several classes of polynomial rings over discrete valuation rings, UFDs and fields. Finally, we characterize additive homeomorphisms between Mac\'ias spaces of certain domains of characteristic zero via ring isomorphisms, partially answering a problem of Mac\'ias and Ortiz (2025).

papers.title: Completions of vector metric spaces and the diagonal property of order convergence
papers.abstract: A vector metric space carries a distance with values in an ordered vector space $E$; a sequence converges if its distances to the limit are dominated by a sequence decreasing to zero in $E$. We show that, for Archimedean $E$, every $E$-valued vector metric space has a completion if and only if order Cauchy sequences in $E$ converge and $E$ has the diagonal property of order convergence (SDP): for every double sequence $(a^k_n)$ with $a^k_n\downarrow_n0$ there are indices $n_k$ and $e_k\downarrow 0$ with $a^k_{n_k}\le e_k$. In vector lattices this is the classical diagonal property of Kantorovich, equivalently the strong Egoroff property. We show that its standard characterisations remain valid in Archimedean ordered vector spaces, and that it holds if and only if convergence in every $E$-valued vector metric space satisfies the iterated limit axiom. For an ordered Banach space with a closed normal cone, all completions exist if and only if the norm is $\sigma$-order continuous; if the cone has an interior point, all vector metrics are then scalar. By a theorem of Veksler and of Hager and van Mill, for compact Hausdorff $K$ either $K$ is an almost $P$-space and $C(K)$-valued vector metrics are scalar, or there are countable $C(K)$-valued vector metric spaces without completion. A product of ordered vector spaces with (SDP) and nonzero cones has (SDP) if and only if there are fewer than $\mathfrak b$ factors, extending a result of Hager and van Mill for $\mathbb{R}^A$. We also prove permanence results for direct summands and uniformly dense vector lattice covers of pre-Riesz spaces.
